alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 27 at 3:58PM HST until September 28 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of Maui, Molokai, Oahu, and the Big Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can tear off shingles, knock down tree
branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.
alerts.instruction:
Watch out for falling tree branches when walking or driving. Make
sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 27 at 3:05PM HST until September 28 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF KAUAI
AND OAHU THROUGH MONDAY MORNING...

.Rough short period east swell is declining from east to west but
will remain large enough to maintain high surf along east facing
shores of Oahu and Kauai overnight.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet.

* WHERE...East facing shores of Kauai and Oahu.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Sun Sep 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located about 155 miles southwest of Cabo San Lazaro, Mexico,
on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred miles southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm Rachel, located a few
hundred miles southwest of southern Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
A broad area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands continues to become better organized. Environmental
conditions are expected to be conducive for further development, and
a tropical depression is likely to form during the next day or so.
The system should move generally northeastward and remain well east
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

aiBriefing: Aktualne ostrzeżenia o silnym wietrze i wysokiej fali na Hawajach wygasają dziś rano (28 września) i powinny zakończyć się zanim zaczniecie podróż 2 października — to jest za 4 dni. Więcej uwagi wymaga huragan Nolo, kategoria 4, który jest obecnie około 626 km od trasy — to wciąż daleko, ale warto śledzić jego rozwój w najbliższych dniach, bo jego tor może się zmienić przed Waszym wylotem. Dodatkowo NWS/CPHC wskazuje na 90% szans uformowania się nowego układu tropikalnego w ciągu 7 dni, ale ten potencjalny system znajduje się daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów i prognozowany jest ruch w kierunku północno-wschodnim, czyli dalej od wysp — na razie nie ma dla Was bezpośredniego zagrożenia z tej strony. Ogólnie poziom zagrożenia jest "Podwyższony" (2), co oznacza, że nic krytycznego się nie dzieje, ale sytuacja w regionie jest aktywna i warto sprawdzać prognozę ponownie bliżej wyjazdu, zwłaszcza w kontekście Nolo.
